hints.title: Impossibility Condition
hints.text: Because operations can only decrease values down to h, if any number is strictly less than k, reaching k is impossible.

hints.title: Distinct Levels Above Target
hints.text: Each unique value strictly greater than k must be reduced down to the next largest value, costing one operation each.

hints.title: Counting Unique Values
hints.text: Count the number of distinct values strictly greater than k; return -1 if any element is smaller than k.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Hash set collects unique values; if min(nums) < k it is impossible, else count unique values strictly greater than k.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating individual operation reductions is slower than counting distinct values directly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) hash set stores distinct array values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that each distinct value strictly greater than k must be reduced in order.
